transcript: Yesterday, my boyfriend Paul and I saw The Gardens of Anuncia at Lincoln Center. It’s a new musical based on the life of Broadway dancer, choreographer, and director Graciela Daniele growing up in Argentina in the 1940s with her mother, her grandmother, and her aunt. And it's directed and choreographed by Graciela herself. This musical is small but mighty with heartfelt music and performances, particularly Mary Testa's comedic performance as Anuncia's grandmother. The show is told through the eyes of Anuncia herself, both younger and older, and we see a series of core memories that taught her about life and love. I would have preferred some more narrative structure because I think the pacing suffered a bit without that kind of momentum but overall this was pretty enjoyable. The Gardens of Anuncia is running through the end of the year at Lincoln Center, so if you wanna see it, now is your chance. With that, another playbill for my collection.
